subject: mathematics
question_text: If a = 2i+3j+4k, b = i+j−k and c = i−j+k, then compute a×(b×c) and verify that it is perpendicular to a.

mark_split.label: Verify the dot product with a is zero

steps.margin_note: First mark. The i component comes out as 0 here — write the 0 rather than leaving a gap, or the next determinant will be misaligned.

steps.why: A zero component is still a component. Writing it keeps the rows of the next determinant lined up under i, j and k.
common_mistakes: Omitting the zero and writing a two-component vector.

steps.label: Find a×(b×c)
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. a on the first row, the bracket result on the second. The zero in the second row kills one product in each expansion.
steps.memory_tip: a on the first row, the bracket result on the second. The zero kills one product in each expansion.

recall.must_convey: That a is crossed into the bracket result to give 2i + 4j − 4k.

steps.why: The vector triple product a×(b×c) is always perpendicular to a — this computation is what the next step will confirm on these particular numbers.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that the j term already carries a minus from the expansion.

steps.label: Verify perpendicular
steps.margin_note: Last mark, and it needs real working. Two vectors are perpendicular exactly when their dot product is zero — so compute the dot product and show it vanishes.
steps.memory_tip: Perpendicular means the DOT product is zero, so compute it and show it vanishes.

steps.why: a×(b×c) is a combination of b and c, and crossing anything with a leaves a result perpendicular to a. The dot product is the check that turns that fact into a marked step.
common_mistakes: Taking a cross product instead of a dot product.
